title: Looking ahead to a project milestone
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Future Perfect Continuous (will have been + -ing), usado para dizer há quanto tempo uma atividade estará acontecendo até um marco futuro. Na Engenharia de Aplicação isso aparece em prazos de comissionamento, campanhas de teste e garantias: 'na partida, já estaremos testando o filtro há seis meses'. É a forma ideal para falar de duração até um ponto no futuro.
intro: Sometimes a project is best described by how long it will have been running when a future milestone arrives. By the commissioning date, we will have been testing the scrubber for six months.

Today we practise the Future Perfect Continuous — will have been + -ing. It is the tense engineers use for warranties, milestones and long test campaigns, when duration up to a future point is the whole story.
introAudio: Hello again. Let us look into the future of a project. By start-up, we will have been running the baghouse for months, and the crew will have been installing the ducts for weeks. Today we learn to say how long an activity will have been going on by a certain point. Let us begin.
vocab: By the commissioning date, the crew will have been testing the ducts for a week.
By start-up, we will have been preparing the system for months.
By the audit, the filter bags will have been capturing dust for a full year.
By December, the plant will have been reporting high uptime for six months.
When the warranty ends, we will have been supporting the client for two years.
By the next milestone, the team will have been running trials for weeks.
practice: By the time we reach ______, the crew will have been testing the ducts for a week.
commissioning
By ______, we will have been preparing the whole system for months.
start-up
By the audit, the ______ will have been filtering dust for a full year.
filter bags
By December, the plant will have been reporting high ______ for six months.
uptime
When the ______ ends, we will have been supporting the client for two years.
warranty
By the next ______, the team will have been running trials for weeks.
milestone
By hand-over, the crew will have been improving the ______ figures steadily.
uptime
By the review, we will have been checking the ______ pressure for days.
filter bags

audio.title: A milestone update
audio.text: Let me look ahead to the commissioning date. By the time the plant starts up, we will have been designing this baghouse for eight months. The site crew will have been installing the ducts for three weeks, and Ana will have been running the acceptance tests since the first week. By the audit in December, we will have been monitoring the emissions for half a year. The client will have been operating the system long enough to trust it. By hand-over, our team will have been supporting this project from the very first drawing.

readAloud: By December, we will have been running the baghouse for a year.
By the time you arrive, the crew will have been installing the ducts since dawn.
By start-up, the team will have been testing the scrubber for six months.
By Friday, I will have been checking the flow calculations for three days.
By 2027, the plant will have been using our system for a decade.
fill: By June, we ___ the baghouse for a year. (run)
will have been running
By the time you arrive, the team ___ the ducts since dawn. (install)
will have been installing
By 2027, the plant ___ our scrubber for a decade. (use)
will have been using
By Friday, I ___ the flow calculations for three days. (check)
will have been checking
By next month, she ___ on the emission report for weeks. (work)
will have been working
By start-up, we ___ the system for six months. (test)
will have been testing
By noon, the fan ___ against a high dust load for hours. (operate)
will have been operating
By the audit, they ___ the datasheets for months. (review)
will have been reviewing
qa: How long will you have been running the baghouse by June?
By June, we will have been running it for a year.
What will the team have been doing by the time the client arrives?
They will have been installing the ducts since dawn.
Will you have been testing the scrubber for long by start-up?
Yes, by start-up we will have been testing it for six months.
How long will she have been working on the emission report by Friday?
By Friday, she will have been working on it for two weeks.
What will the plant have been doing by 2027?
By 2027, it will have been using our system for a decade.

a.label: A frase deve conter 'will have been'
a.placeholder: By June, we will have been running ...

b.label: A frase deve começar com 'by'
b.placeholder: By the audit, the team will have been ...

sentences: By June, we will have been running the baghouse for a year.
By the commissioning date, the crew will have been installing the ducts for a week.
By start-up, the team will have been testing the scrubber for six months.
By Friday, I will have been checking the flow calculations for three days.
By next month, she will have been working on the emission report for weeks.
By 2027, the plant will have been using our system for a decade.
By noon, the fan will have been operating against a high dust load for hours.
By the audit, they will have been reviewing the datasheets for months.
grammarPoint: O Future Perfect Continuous — will have been + verbo-ing — descreve por quanto tempo uma ação já estará em andamento até um ponto no futuro. Costuma vir com by (até) + for (duração) ou since (início). By June, we will have been running the baghouse for a year. — Em junho, já faremos um ano operando o filtro de manga. She will have been testing it since Monday. — Ela estará testando desde segunda.
deepDive: A estrutura é fixa: will have been + verbo com -ing, igual para todas as pessoas (I, you, he, she, we, they) — os modais não mudam. Use for para a duração (for six months) e since para o ponto de início (since Monday). Diferença útil: o Future Perfect simples (will have finished) enfatiza a conclusão; o Future Perfect Continuous (will have been running) enfatiza a duração até aquele momento. Ideal para prazos de garantia, comissionamento e marcos de projeto.
examples: By June, we will have been running the baghouse for a year.
Em junho, já faremos um ano operando o filtro de manga.
By start-up, the team will have been testing the scrubber for six months.
Na partida, a equipe já estará testando o lavador há seis meses.
By Friday, I will have been checking the calculations for three days.
Até sexta, eu já estarei conferindo os cálculos há três dias.
By 2027, the plant will have been using our system for a decade.
Até 2027, a planta já estará usando nosso sistema há uma década.
By noon, the fan will have been operating for hours.
Ao meio-dia, o ventilador já estará operando há horas.
By the audit, they will have been reviewing the datasheets for months.
Até a auditoria, eles já estarão revisando as folhas de dados há meses.
By next week, she will have been working on the memo since Monday.
Na semana que vem, ela já estará trabalhando no memorial desde segunda.
By hand-over, we will have been supporting the client for two years.
Até a entrega, já estaremos dando suporte ao cliente há dois anos.
mistakes: By June, we will have been run it for a year.
By June, we will have been running it for a year.
Depois de been o verbo leva -ing.
By June, we will has been running it.
By June, we will have been running it.
Com will use sempre have, nunca has.
By June, we will have been running it since a year.
By June, we will have been running it for a year.
Duração pede for, não since.
By June, we are going to have been running it.
By June, we will have been running it.
A estrutura fixa é will have been + -ing.
By June, she will have been work here for months.
By June, she will have been working here for months.
Falta o -ing no verbo principal.
quick: By June, we ___ the baghouse for a year. (run)
By dawn, the crew ___ the ducts for hours. (install)
By 2027, the plant ___ our scrubber for a decade. (use)
By Friday, I ___ the calculations for three days. (check)
By start-up, we ___ the system for six months. (test)

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now describe how long a project will have been running by any future milestone — the language of commissioning and warranties.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você sabe dizer há quanto tempo um projeto estará em andamento até qualquer marco futuro — a linguagem do comissionamento e das garantias.

title: Explaining the purpose behind a design
grammar: Propósito e resultado — to / in order to / so that
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a expressar propósito e resultado com to, in order to e so that. Na Engenharia de Aplicação você justifica cada decisão de projeto: superdimensionamos o ventilador para lidar com o pico de vazão, adicionamos um ciclone para que as mangas durem mais. Essas estruturas deixam suas propostas e memoriais claros sobre o porquê de cada escolha.
intro: Every design decision has a reason. We oversized the fan to handle peak flow. We added a pre-cyclone in order to protect the bags. We raised the stack so that the plume disperses better.
Today we practise three ways to explain purpose: to + verb, in order to + verb, and so that + clause. They turn a list of choices into a clear, well-argued proposal.
introAudio: Welcome back. Engineers must always explain why. We seal the ducts to stop leaks, and we add a spare fan in order to keep the plant running. We raise the stack so that the gas disperses well. Today we learn to give reasons clearly. Let us start.
vocab: We oversized the fan to handle the peak flow.
We seal every joint so that no air leak reduces the suction.
We raised the stack in order to improve dispersion.
We ordered early in order to cut the lead time.
We added a spare fan for redundancy so that the plant never stops.
We tightened the design to guarantee compliance with the limit.
practice: We oversized the fan to handle the ______ during full production.
peak flow
We sealed every joint so that no ______ reduces the suction.
air leak
We raised the stack in order to improve the ______ of the clean gas.
dispersion
We ordered the fans early in order to cut the ______ from the supplier.
lead time
We added a spare fan for ______ so that the plant never stops.
redundancy
We tightened the design in order to guarantee ______ with the limit.
compliance
We monitor the ______ closely to protect the filter bags.
peak flow
We test every weld so that no ______ appears later.
air leak

audio.title: Explaining the design choices
audio.text: Let me explain why we designed the system this way. We oversized the fan in order to handle the peak flow during full production. We added a pre-cyclone to reduce the dust load, so that the filter bags last much longer. We sealed every duct joint to prevent air leaks that would waste suction. We raised the stack in order to improve dispersion and meet the emission limit. Finally, we specified a spare fan so that the plant keeps running during maintenance. Every choice has a clear purpose.

readAloud: We oversized the fan to handle the peak flow.
We added a pre-cyclone in order to protect the filter bags.
We raised the stack so that the plume disperses better.
We sealed the ducts to prevent air leaks.
We ordered the fans early in order to cut the lead time.
fill: We oversized the fan ___ handle peak flow. (purpose, short)
to
We added a cyclone ___ the bags would last longer. (result clause)
so that
We met the supplier ___ speed up the delivery. (formal purpose)
in order to
We sealed the ducts ___ prevent air leaks. (purpose, short)
to
We raised the stack ___ the gas disperses better. (result clause)
so that
We double-checked the sizing ___ avoid a costly error. (formal purpose)
in order to
We labelled every valve ___ operators find them fast. (result clause)
so that
We ran a trial ___ confirm the flow rate. (purpose, short)
to
qa: Why did you oversize the fan?
We oversized it to handle the peak flow.
Why did you add a pre-cyclone?
We added it in order to protect the filter bags.
Why did you raise the stack?
We raised it so that the plume disperses better.
Why did you seal every joint?
We sealed them to prevent air leaks.
Why did you order the fans early?
We ordered them early so that we could cut the lead time.

a.label: A frase deve conter 'in order to'
a.placeholder: We raised the stack in order to ...

b.label: A frase deve conter 'so that'
b.placeholder: We added a cyclone so that ...

sentences: We oversized the fan to handle the peak flow.
We added a pre-cyclone in order to protect the filter bags.
We raised the stack so that the plume disperses better.
We sealed every joint to prevent air leaks.
We ordered the fans early in order to cut the lead time.
We specified a spare fan so that the plant never stops.
We double-checked the sizing in order to avoid a costly error.
We labelled each valve so that operators can find it quickly.
grammarPoint: Para explicar propósito (o porquê), use to + verbo ou, mais formal, in order to + verbo, ambos seguidos do verbo na forma base. Para propósito ou resultado com um novo sujeito, use so that + oração (sujeito + verbo). We raised the stack to improve dispersion. — Elevamos a chaminé para melhorar a dispersão. We added a cyclone so that the bags last longer. — Adicionamos um ciclone para que as mangas durem mais.
deepDive: to + verbo é a forma mais comum e neutra; in order to soa mais formal, ótimo para memoriais. Ambos precisam do MESMO sujeito nas duas partes: We sealed the ducts to stop leaks (nós selamos, nós paramos). Quando o segundo sujeito é diferente, use so that + oração completa: We raised the stack so that the gas disperses. Cuidado: nunca use for + verbo para propósito de uma ação (errado: for to stop, for stopping); use to stop.
examples: We oversized the fan to handle the peak flow.
Superdimensionamos o ventilador para lidar com a vazão de pico.
We added a pre-cyclone in order to protect the bags.
Adicionamos um pré-ciclone para proteger as mangas.
We raised the stack so that the plume disperses.
Elevamos a chaminé para que a pluma se disperse.
We sealed the ducts to prevent air leaks.
Selamos os dutos para evitar vazamentos de ar.
We ordered early in order to cut the lead time.
Compramos com antecedência para reduzir o prazo de entrega.
We added a spare fan so that the plant never stops.
Adicionamos um ventilador reserva para que a planta nunca pare.
We checked the sizing to avoid a costly error.
Conferimos o dimensionamento para evitar um erro caro.
We labelled the valves so that the crew finds them fast.
Etiquetamos as válvulas para que a equipe as ache rápido.
mistakes: We oversized the fan for handle the flow.
We oversized the fan to handle the flow.
Propósito de uma ação usa to + verbo, não for.
We added a cyclone for protecting the bags.
We added a cyclone to protect the bags.
Evite for + -ing para propósito; use to + verbo.
We raised the stack so that disperse the gas.
We raised the stack so that the gas disperses.
Depois de so that vem sujeito + verbo.
We sealed the ducts in order stop leaks.
We sealed the ducts in order to stop leaks.
A forma é in order TO + verbo.
We ordered early for to cut the lead time.
We ordered early to cut the lead time.
'for to' não existe; use apenas to.
quick: We added a cyclone ___ protect the bags. (short)
We raised the stack ___ the gas disperses well. (clause)
We met the supplier ___ speed up delivery. (formal)
We sealed the ducts ___ stop leaks. (short)
We labelled the valves ___ the crew finds them. (clause)

celebrate.en: Excellent. You can now justify every design choice with a clear purpose — the mark of a convincing proposal.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você justifica cada escolha de projeto com um propósito claro — a marca de uma proposta convincente.

title: Investigating failures across time
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender as condicionais mistas, que combinam um tempo na condição e outro no resultado — perfeitas para o troubleshooting hipotético. Na Engenharia de Aplicação você analisa falhas assim: 'se tivéssemos especificado um ventilador maior, o sistema não estaria sofrendo agora'. Elas ligam uma decisão passada a uma consequência presente, ou uma característica atual a um resultado passado.
intro: When we investigate a problem, we often mix time frames. If we had specified a bigger fan, the system would not be struggling now. If the bags were the right grade, they would not have failed last week.

Today we practise mixed conditionals. One type links a past condition to a present result; the other links a present, always-true condition to a past result. Both are essential for honest technical troubleshooting.
introAudio: Hello again. Troubleshooting often mixes past and present. If we had chosen a scrubber, the emissions would be lower now. If the fan were bigger, it would have handled last week's overload. Today we learn these mixed conditionals. Let us begin.
vocab: If we had planned for the overload, the fan would not be at its limit now.
If the team had found the root cause, we would have the fix today.
If the drawing had a wider tolerance, the parts would fit now.
If we kept this spare part in stock, we would have replaced it last night.
If we had approved the retrofit, the plant would meet the limit now.
If the sensor were reliable, it would have caught the fault yesterday.
practice: If we had planned for the ______, the fan would not be at its limit now.
overload
If the team had found the ______ sooner, we would have the fix today.
root cause
If the drawing had a wider ______, the parts would fit now.
tolerance
If we kept a ______ in stock, we would have replaced it last night.
spare part
If we had approved the ______, the plant would meet the limit now.
retrofit
If the sensor were reliable, it would have caught the ______ yesterday.
fault
If we had sized for the peak ______, the system would cope now.
overload
If they had documented the ______, we would know the answer today.
root cause

audio.title: Investigating a performance problem
audio.text: Let me walk you through the troubleshooting. The baghouse is losing suction today. If we had specified a bigger fan last year, the system would not be struggling now. The filter bags failed early; if they were the correct grade, they would not have failed so soon. The client sent the data late; if they had sent it on time, we would already have the answer today. The pressure drop is still high, so if the ducts were properly sealed, we would have found the leak much earlier. If we had approved the retrofit, the plant would easily meet the limit today.

readAloud: If we had oversized the fan, the plant would run better now.
If the bags were the right grade, they would not have failed last month.
If we had chosen a scrubber, the emissions would be within limits now.
If the fan were bigger, it would have handled last week's overload.
If they had followed the datasheet, the filter would work properly today.
fill: If we had oversized the fan, the plant ___ better now. (run)
would run
If the bags were the right grade, they ___ last month. (not fail)
would not have failed
If the client had sent the data, we ___ the answer today. (have)
would have
If the ducts were properly sealed, we ___ the leak last week. (not miss)
would not have missed
If we had chosen a scrubber, the emissions ___ within limits now. (be)
would be
If the fan were bigger, it ___ last week's overload. (handle)
would have handled
If they had followed the datasheet, the filter ___ properly today. (work)
would work
If the temperature were lower, the bags ___ so fast last year. (not degrade)
would not have degraded
qa: Why is the system struggling now?
If we had specified a bigger fan, it would not be struggling now.
Why did the bags fail so early?
If they were the right grade, they would not have failed so early.
Why don't we have the answer yet?
If the client had sent the data, we would already have it today.
Why are the emissions still high?
If we had approved the retrofit, they would be within limits now.
Why did the sensor miss the fault?
If the sensor were reliable, it would have caught the fault yesterday.

a.label: A frase deve conter 'would'
a.placeholder: If we had sized it right, the fan would ...

b.label: A frase deve conter 'had'
b.placeholder: If we had approved the retrofit, ...

sentences: If we had oversized the fan, the plant would run better now.
If the bags were the right grade, they would not have failed last month.
If the client had sent the data, we would have the answer today.
If the ducts were properly sealed, we would not have missed the leak.
If we had chosen a scrubber, the emissions would be within limits now.
If the fan were bigger, it would have handled last week's overload.
If they had followed the datasheet, the filter would work properly today.
If we kept a spare part in stock, we would have replaced it last night.
grammarPoint: As condicionais mistas combinam tempos diferentes na condição e no resultado. Tipo 1 (passado to presente): If + past perfect, would + verbo base. If we had sized it correctly, the fan would work now. — Se tivéssemos dimensionado certo, o ventilador funcionaria agora. Tipo 2 (presente to passado): If + past simple, would have + particípio. If the bags were better, they would not have failed. — Se as mangas fossem melhores, não teriam falhado.
deepDive: Pense no tempo da CONDIÇÃO e no tempo do RESULTADO separadamente. Causa no passado com efeito agora: If we had approved the retrofit (passado), the plant would meet the limit now (presente). Característica sempre-verdadeira com efeito no passado: If the fan were bigger (presente/geral), it would have handled the overload (passado). Com o verbo to be na condição, o inglês formal usa were para todas as pessoas (if the fan were bigger). Palavras como now, today, last week ajudam a marcar o tempo de cada parte.
examples: If we had oversized the fan, the plant would run better now.
Se tivéssemos superdimensionado o ventilador, a planta funcionaria melhor agora.
If the bags were the right grade, they would not have failed.
Se as mangas fossem do tipo certo, não teriam falhado.
If the client had sent the data, we would have the answer today.
Se o cliente tivesse enviado os dados, teríamos a resposta hoje.
If the fan were bigger, it would have handled the overload.
Se o ventilador fosse maior, teria aguentado a sobrecarga.
If we had chosen a scrubber, emissions would be lower now.
Se tivéssemos escolhido um lavador, as emissões estariam menores agora.
If the sensor were reliable, it would have caught the fault.
Se o sensor fosse confiável, teria detectado a falha.
If they had read the datasheet, the filter would work now.
Se tivessem lido a folha de dados, o filtro funcionaria agora.
If we kept spares in stock, we would have fixed it last night.
Se mantivéssemos peças no estoque, teríamos consertado ontem à noite.
mistakes: If we had oversized the fan, the plant will run better now.
If we had oversized the fan, the plant would run better now.
No resultado use would, não will.
If we would have sized it right, it would work now.
If we had sized it right, it would work now.
Na condição use had + particípio, não 'would have'.
If the bags were right, they would not failed.
If the bags were right, they would not have failed.
Resultado no passado pede would have + particípio.
If the fan was bigger, it would have coped.
If the fan were bigger, it would have coped.
No inglês formal use were para todas as pessoas.
If the client sent the data, we would have the answer today.
If the client had sent the data, we would have the answer today.
Causa no passado pede past perfect (had sent).
quick: If we had oversized the fan, the plant ___ better now. (run)
If the bags were right, they ___ last month. (not fail)
If we had chosen a scrubber, emissions ___ low now. (be)
If the fan were bigger, it ___ the overload yesterday. (handle)
If they had read the datasheet, it ___ now. (work)

celebrate.en: Great work. You can now reason about failures across time — exactly how a good engineer explains root causes.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você raciocina sobre falhas cruzando tempos — exatamente como um bom engenheiro explica causas raiz.

title: What each component makes, lets and enables
grammar: make / let / allow / enable + objeto + verbo
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar make, let, allow e enable com objeto + verbo para descrever o que um componente permite, impede ou possibilita. Na Engenharia de Aplicação isso é essencial: um registro de desvio deixa o gás passar ao redor do filtro, um inversor permite que o ventilador acompanhe a vazão. Você vai dominar a diferença entre make/let (verbo base) e allow/enable (to + verbo).
intro: Good design is about control: what a part makes happen, what it lets happen, and what it allows people to do. The bypass damper lets the gas flow around the filter. The new controller allows operators to adjust the fan remotely.
Today we practise make, let, allow and enable. The tricky part is the verb form after the object: make and let take the bare verb, while allow and enable take to + verb.
introAudio: Welcome back. Engineers describe what each part does to the process. The pre-cyclone makes the dust drop, the interlock does not let the fan start unsafely, and the new drive enables the system to match the flow. Notice: make and let take the base verb, allow and enable take to. Let us practise.
vocab: The bypass damper lets the hot gas flow around the baghouse.
The interlock does not let the fan start without the damper open.
The access hatch allows the crew to replace the bags easily.
The variable-speed drive enables the fan to match the flow rate.
A taller stack makes the plume disperse more widely.
The controller allows the operator to adjust the damper remotely.
practice: The ______ lets the hot gas flow around the baghouse.
bypass damper
The ______ does not let the fan start without permission.
interlock
The ______ allows the crew to replace the bags easily.
access hatch
The ______ enables the fan to match the flow rate.
variable-speed drive
A taller stack makes the ______ disperse more widely.
plume
The ______ allows the operator to adjust the damper remotely.
controller
The ______ lets the technician reach the tube sheet safely.
access hatch
The ______ makes the motor run only when it is safe.
interlock

audio.title: What each part does
audio.text: Let me explain how the system stays under control. The bypass damper lets the hot gas flow around the baghouse during start-up, so the bags never overheat. The interlock does not let the fan start unless the inlet damper is open. The new variable-speed drive enables the fan to match the exact flow rate, which saves energy. A large access hatch allows the crew to replace the filter bags in a single shift. Finally, the taller stack makes the clean plume disperse well above the plant. Every feature makes the operator's job safer and easier.

readAloud: The bypass damper lets the gas flow around the filter.
The interlock does not let the fan start unsafely.
The new controller allows operators to monitor the pressure drop.
The variable-speed drive enables the fan to match the flow.
A taller stack makes the plume disperse more widely.
fill: The bypass damper lets the gas ___ around the filter. (flow)
flow
The new controller allows operators ___ the pressure drop remotely. (monitor)
to monitor
A taller stack makes the plume ___ more widely. (disperse)
disperse
This design enables the plant ___ the emission limit. (meet)
to meet
The interlock does not let the fan ___ without the damper open. (start)
start
The access door allows the crew ___ the bags quickly. (replace)
to replace
The pre-cyclone makes the dust load ___ before the filter. (drop)
drop
The bigger motor enables the system ___ peak flow. (handle)
to handle
qa: What does the bypass damper let the gas do?
It lets the gas flow around the filter.
What does the new controller allow operators to do?
It allows them to monitor the pressure drop remotely.
What does the variable-speed drive enable the fan to do?
It enables the fan to match the flow rate.
What does a taller stack make the plume do?
It makes the plume disperse more widely.
What does the interlock not let the fan do?
It does not let the fan start without the damper open.

a.label: A frase deve conter 'lets'
a.placeholder: The damper lets the gas flow ...

sentences: The bypass damper lets the gas flow around the filter.
The interlock does not let the fan start unsafely.
The new controller allows operators to monitor the pressure drop.
The variable-speed drive enables the fan to match the flow rate.
A taller stack makes the plume disperse more widely.
The access hatch allows the crew to replace the bags quickly.
The pre-cyclone makes the dust load drop before the filter.
The bigger motor enables the system to handle peak flow.
grammarPoint: Estas quatro palavras seguem objeto + verbo, mas em duas formas. make e let usam o verbo na forma BASE (sem to): The damper lets the gas flow. — O registro deixa o gás passar. The stack makes the plume disperse. — A chaminé faz a pluma se dispersar. allow e enable usam TO + verbo: The drive allows the fan to match the flow. — O inversor permite que o ventilador acompanhe a vazão. This design enables the plant to meet the limit. — Este projeto possibilita a planta atender ao limite.
deepDive: Grave o padrão: make/let + objeto + verbo base; allow/enable + objeto + TO + verbo. make significa 'forçar/fazer com que'; let significa 'deixar/permitir' (informal); allow é 'permitir' (mais formal); enable é 'possibilitar/capacitar', ótimo para dizer que um recurso técnico torna algo possível. Cuidado com a voz passiva de make: aí aparece o to — The fan is made to run only when safe. Mas na ativa, nada de to depois de make e let.
examples: The bypass damper lets the gas flow around the filter.
O registro de desvio deixa o gás passar ao redor do filtro.
The interlock does not let the fan start unsafely.
O intertravamento não deixa o ventilador partir de forma insegura.
The controller allows operators to monitor the pressure drop.
O controlador permite que os operadores monitorem a perda de carga.
The drive enables the fan to match the flow rate.
O inversor possibilita que o ventilador acompanhe a vazão.
A taller stack makes the plume disperse more widely.
Uma chaminé mais alta faz a pluma se dispersar mais amplamente.
The access hatch allows the crew to replace the bags.
A escotilha de acesso permite que a equipe troque as mangas.
The pre-cyclone makes the dust load drop.
O pré-ciclone faz a carga de poeira cair.
The bigger motor enables the system to handle peak flow.
O motor maior possibilita o sistema lidar com a vazão de pico.
mistakes: The damper lets the gas to flow around the filter.
The damper lets the gas flow around the filter.
Depois de let o verbo fica na base, sem to.
The stack makes the plume to disperse.
The stack makes the plume disperse.
Depois de make (ativo) não use to.
The controller allows operators monitor the pressure.
The controller allows operators to monitor the pressure.
allow pede to + verbo.
The drive enables the fan matching the flow.
The drive enables the fan to match the flow.
enable pede to + verbo, não -ing.
The design lets the plant to meet the limit.
The design enables the plant to meet the limit.
Com to use allow/enable; let não leva to.
quick: The damper lets the gas ___ freely. (flow)
The PLC allows us ___ the pressure. (monitor)
The stack makes the plume ___ well. (disperse)
The design enables the plant ___ the limit. (meet)
The interlock does not let the fan ___ early. (start)

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now describe exactly what each component makes, lets, allows or enables — the precise language of technical design.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você descreve exatamente o que cada componente faz, deixa, permite ou possibilita — a linguagem precisa do projeto técnico.

title: Fixed prepositions on a datasheet
grammar: Preposições dependentes (responsible for, capable of, consists of, results in)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender preposições dependentes fixas: responsible for, capable of, consists of, results in e outras. Na Engenharia de Aplicação você escreve isso o tempo todo: 'o engenheiro é responsável pelo dimensionamento', 'o sistema é composto por um ciclone e um filtro', 'um duto entupido resulta em maior perda de carga'. Usar a preposição certa deixa seus datasheets e memoriais corretos e profissionais.
intro: Some words in English always take a fixed preposition. The engineer is responsible for the sizing. This fan is capable of high pressure. The system consists of several units, and a blocked duct results in a higher pressure drop.
Today we practise these dependent prepositions. There is little logic to them — you learn them as fixed pairs — but getting them right makes your technical English sound native.
introAudio: Hello again. Technical English is full of fixed pairs. We are responsible for the design, the fan is capable of high flow, the system consists of three units, and a leak results in higher emissions. Today we learn these dependent prepositions. Let us begin.
vocab: The application engineer is responsible for the equipment sizing.
This fan is capable of moving sixty thousand cubic metres per hour.
The system consists of a cyclone and a baghouse.
A clogged filter results in a high pressure drop.
The right choice depends on the gas temperature.
The proposal is based on the client's process data.
practice: The application engineer is ______ the whole sizing calculation.
responsible for
This baghouse is ______ handling a very high dust load.
capable of
The dust collection system ______ a cyclone, a filter and a fan.
consists of
A leaking gasket ______ higher emissions at the stack.
results in
The final equipment choice ______ the process temperature.
depends on
Our proposal is ______ the flow data from the site visit.
based on
The site team is ______ the safe erection of the ducts.
responsible for
A blocked screw conveyor ______ unplanned downtime.
results in

audio.title: Describing the system on a datasheet
audio.text: Let me summarise the datasheet. The application engineer is responsible for the sizing and the equipment selection. The dust collection system consists of a cyclone, a baghouse and an induced-draught fan. The fan is capable of moving sixty thousand cubic metres per hour against a high static pressure. The final choice of filter media depends on the gas temperature and the dust type. A worn gasket usually results in higher emissions at the stack, so the whole crew is responsible for regular inspection. Every figure here is based on the process data from the site visit.

readAloud: The application engineer is responsible for the sizing.
This baghouse is capable of handling a high dust load.
The system consists of a cyclone, a filter and a fan.
A blocked duct results in a higher pressure drop.
The final choice depends on the gas temperature.
fill: The application engineer is responsible ___ the sizing. (preposition)
for
This baghouse is capable ___ handling 50,000 cubic metres per hour. (preposition)
of
The system consists ___ a cyclone, a filter and a fan. (preposition)
of
A blocked duct results ___ a higher pressure drop. (preposition)
in
The final choice depends ___ the process temperature. (preposition)
on
The design is based ___ the client's flow data. (preposition)
on
This scrubber is suitable ___ acidic gases. (preposition)
for
The whole crew is responsible ___ site safety. (preposition)
for
qa: Who is responsible for the sizing?
The application engineer is responsible for it.
Is this fan capable of high pressure?
Yes, it is capable of a high static pressure.
What does the system consist of?
It consists of a cyclone, a filter and a fan.
What does a blocked duct result in?
It results in a higher pressure drop.
What does the final choice depend on?
It depends on the gas temperature and the dust type.
sentences: The application engineer is responsible for the sizing.
This baghouse is capable of handling a high dust load.
The system consists of a cyclone, a filter and a fan.
A blocked duct results in a higher pressure drop.
The final choice depends on the gas temperature.
The whole proposal is based on the site data.
The site team is responsible for the safe erection of the ducts.
A worn gasket results in higher emissions at the stack.
grammarPoint: Muitos adjetivos e verbos exigem uma preposição fixa, que deve ser memorizada. responsible for (responsável por), capable of (capaz de), consists of (é composto por), results in (resulta em), depends on (depende de), based on (baseado em). The engineer is responsible for the sizing. — O engenheiro é responsável pelo dimensionamento. The system consists of three units. — O sistema é composto por três unidades.
deepDive: Não traduza a preposição do português — memorize o par. Cuidado com os erros clássicos: responsible FOR (não 'of'), capable OF (não 'to'), consist OF (não 'in'), result IN (não 'on'), depend ON (não 'of'). Depois de of o verbo aparece na forma -ing: capable of moving, capable of handling. Já result in e depend on costumam vir seguidos de substantivo: results in downtime, depends on the temperature.
examples: The engineer is responsible for the sizing.
O engenheiro é responsável pelo dimensionamento.
This fan is capable of high static pressure.
Este ventilador é capaz de alta pressão estática.
The system consists of three main units.
O sistema é composto por três unidades principais.
A blocked duct results in a higher pressure drop.
Um duto entupido resulta em maior perda de carga.
The choice depends on the gas temperature.
A escolha depende da temperatura do gás.
The proposal is based on the process data.
A proposta é baseada nos dados de processo.
This scrubber is suitable for acidic gases.
Este lavador é adequado para gases ácidos.
The crew is responsible for site safety.
A equipe é responsável pela segurança no canteiro.
mistakes: The engineer is responsible of the sizing.
The engineer is responsible for the sizing.
responsible pede for, não of.
This fan is capable to move the gas.
This fan is capable of moving the gas.
capable pede of + verbo-ing, não to.
The system consists in three units.
The system consists of three units.
consist pede of, não in.
A blocked duct results on a higher pressure drop.
A blocked duct results in a higher pressure drop.
result pede in, não on.
The choice depends of the temperature.
The choice depends on the temperature.
depend pede on, não of.
quick: The engineer is responsible ___ the datasheet. (preposition)
The fan is capable ___ high static pressure. (preposition)
A worn bag results ___ dust leakage. (preposition)
The sizing depends ___ the flow rate. (preposition)

celebrate.en: Excellent. Your datasheets and memos now use the exact prepositions a native engineer would — a real mark of fluency.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Seus datasheets e memoriais agora usam exatamente as preposições que um engenheiro nativo usaria — uma verdadeira marca de fluência.
